answer: Each AI agent posts a signed proof of stake to a distributed ledger that records its identity on a virtual canyon of cryptographic hashes. Peers periodically audit by challenging neighboring agents on a knoll of randomly selected slots; if an agent cannot produce the required bond, its stake is slashed and its terrace of reputation is removed, making a Sybil cost proportional to the total bonded value. An attacker therefore must lock up and risk forfeiting the full bond for every fake node, scaling linearly with the number of identities.
